- If possible, please confirm any PO / procurement timeline so we can align the implementation window.

I’ll summarize key change points for internal stakeholders after I hear back.

Action items I propose:

2) Laura: can you confirm whether security acceptance (Exhibit C) requires new evidence beyond our SOC2 + penetration test report? If so, we should pre-share the checklist.
3) Ops: I’ll coordinate implementation windows but need to know if we can reserve a burst pool for them in July (tentative).

I attached a short redline summary I’ll share on the call.

Rachel / team —

Thanks for the heads-up. Quick legal notes (pre-call):
- Section refs: 4.2 (commit) / 7.1 (termination for convenience) / Exhibit B (fee bands). We should avoid open-ended rollback language; propose a "grace rebalancing" clause limited to a single 90-day window with clearly defined metrics (documented traffic and error rate thresholds) and a one-time adjustment to the committed units. That keeps exposure contained.
- Acceptance criteria: suggest we reuse our standard Exhibit C baseline but add a short pilot checklist (network ingress/outbound ports, KMS integration confirmation, retention settings). Laura — that checklist should be 1 page.
- Commercial: if BrightLoop wants an explicit rollback, we should tie it to a fee recapture cap (e.g., no more than 20% of three months' fees).

Ops note: Jonas, please confirm whether we can tentatively reserve the burst pool for early July and what lead time you need to adjust quantization/VM sizing.

I’ll be on the legal call tomorrow if scheduling works.

-Karthik
